Field guide 44

Access Control This is the mechanics of the Warden, the access system. Aggregation Returns a single object of computed values across all matching rows. Audit Logging Litestone provides field-level and model-level audit logging via the logger database driver. CLI Reference bunx litestone <command> [flags] Concurrency bun:sqlite is synchronous. Every query blocks the thread that issued it — Edge fields — `@edge` / `@scoped` Attach a field value to a relationship instead of a row. Encryption Litestone provides field-level protection at rest. Numbers — `@scale`, `@money`, `@big` and `@unit` .lite has Int and Float and nothing between them, and SQLite has no Bulk export > @@export(ndjson | csv [, since: <column>]) — on a model or on a view. Extensible columns — a field the tenant declares Every CRM, help desk, ATS and marketing tool has the same pair: a customer of your app adds a field at three o'clock on a Tuesday,… File Storage The FileStorage plugin stores file bytes in S3-compatible object storage (Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, AWS S3, MinIO) or local… Filtering // Equality Full-Text Search Litestone builds FTS5 virtual tables and sync triggers automatically for full text search. Where a row is — `@point` A coordinate is two numbers that have to be indexed separately and read as one. Getting Started bun add @frontierjs/litestone Gotchas Production surprises and things that behave differently than you'd expect. Importing a schema litestone import reads a schema you already have into .lite — a Prisma Litestone internals Why the code is shaped the way it is. Typed JSON columns A type is a reusable shape for JSON values. JSON Schema output generateJsonSchema(schema, options) turns a parsed .lite schema into one JSON Migrations Litestone uses two migration modes: autoMigrate for development (like prisma db push) and file-based migrations for production… Modeling decisions Reference tells you what an attribute does. Multi-Database A single Litestone schema can route models to multiple SQLite databases, append-only JSONL log files, and auto-schema audit… Multi-Tenancy One declaration, in the seed. A tenancy { } block at the top of onQuery — Production Query Logging onQuery gives you visibility into every SQL query Litestone executes. Performance Litestone is designed for SQLite's single-writer, multi-reader model. Publishing Notes on publishing @frontierjs/litestone to npm. Querying // Return all matching rows The .lite language, word by word <!-- generated by: litestone catalog --reference --> Relations model Account { Replication Litestone wraps Litestream for continuous WAL replication to S3-compatible storage. Schema Schemas live in .lite files. Syntax is close to Prisma's SDL with SQLite-native extensions. Sequences @sequence provides per-scope auto-increment — a counter that restarts for each unique value of a scope field. Soft Delete Add @@softDelete to a model and Litestone handles all the details: filtering, restore, cascades, and partial indexes. Sorting An orderBy key must be something SQLite can put in an ORDER BY: a stored Litestone Studio Litestone Studio is the browser UI. Testing Litestone ships a /testing subpath with everything needed for fast, deterministic test suites: in-memory clients, factories,… Traits A trait is a reusable model fragment — a chunk of fields and model-level attributes that get spliced into a model via @@trait(T). TypeScript Litestone is written in JavaScript but ships full TypeScript support via generated declarations. `litestone validate` — which stored rows would this schema refuse? Every constraint here is enforced twice. What a row means — `@vector` An embedding is a fixed-length list of float32 that is compared by angle rather Warden The Warden is FrontierJS's access system: everything that decides whether a call Why Litestone There are good ORMs already. Here's why you'd choose Litestone specifically. Window Functions Window functions add computed columns to each row based on a surrounding set of rows (the "window").

The surface, as its README groups it 45

Why In most stacks, your data model is described in five places — an ORM schema, a validator library, TypeScript types, middleware for access control,… How it compares The comparison is organized around what you can declare in the schema and what derives from those declarations. Quick start bunx litestone init # create schema.lite + litestone.config.js Schema Schemas live in a .lite file. Syntax is close to Prisma's SDL with SQLite-native additions. Multi-database Route models to separate SQLite files, JSONL logs, or auto-schema audit loggers: Multi-tenancy Declared in the seed, one block, two strategies. @@external — querying tables Litestone doesn't own @@external marks a model whose table is managed outside Litestone — a SQLite view, an FTS5 virtual table, a table created by a migration tool, or a… createClient import { createClient } from '@frontierjs/litestone' Row-level policies @@allow and @@deny compile to SQL WHERE injections — filtering happens in SQLite, not JS: Access control — GatePlugin Level-based access control. Assign levels 0–9, declare required levels per operation: @system and @guarded — two halves of one grid Only one of the two touches reads: @@transitions — a state machine at the Data boundary An enum field whose legal moves are declared, enforced on every write, and @version — optimistic concurrency model Order { @@scope — a named predicate a caller can ask for The policy compiler, made explicit and opt-in: @derived — a value SQLite computes, so you can filter and sort by it model Task { @@hasTemplates — definition versus instance A category most apps grow by hand: rows that are a definition sitting in the Encryption model User { Query API db.user.findMany({ where, orderBy, limit, offset, include, select, withDeleted,… onQuery — production query logging const db = await createClient({ path: './schema.lite', The audit trail — @@log records a write, $audit records an event @@log(audit) covers writes, which means the events an application most Write events — $tapEvents Every write announces, and the event says whether it can name its row: Is this a valid filter? — $checkWhere / $checkOrderBy A layer above needs to grade a caller-supplied where or orderBy before Migrations import { create, apply, status, verify, autoMigrate } from '@frontierjs/litestone' Schema functions Reusable named SQL expressions — define once, use on any model: @sequence — per-scope auto-increment model Quote { @from — derived relation fields Computed aggregates and lookups from related models — evaluated at query time, not stored. aggregate() and groupBy() // Simple aggregate Recursive tree queries Self-referential models (a field referencing the same model) automatically support CTE-based tree traversal: Window functions Window functions add computed columns to each row based on a set of surrounding rows — rankings, running totals, moving averages, period comparisons. query() — unified dispatcher Routes a single args object to findMany, groupBy, or aggregate based on its shape. Scopes Reusable named query fragments registered per model. Data changes are not migrations migrations/ holds .sql only; a .js file there is refused by migrate create, check and apply with a nonzero exit (FJS-D518). Computed fields // computed.js File storage — FileStorage plugin import { FileStorage, fileUrl, fileUrls, useStorage } from '@frontierjs/litestone' ExternalRefPlugin — custom external-backed fields FileStorage is built on ExternalRefPlugin, a base class for any field whose value is stored outside SQLite. Testing utilities Litestone is the Testing realm's Data half. SQLite utilities // Hot backup — safe during writes Litestone Studio bunx litestone studio # → http://localhost:8502 Shipping a schema change A schema change is a deploy question before it is a migration, and CLI reference litestone init scaffold schema.lite + litestone.config.js Standalone binary The CLI compiles to a single executable with bun build --compile. Single-file library build Separately from the CLI binary, the library bundles to one file. Multi-file schemas // schema.lite Litestream Litestone sets the pragmas Litestream requires (WAL, synchronous=NORMAL, busytimeout=5000 — createClient({ busyTimeout }) or LITESTONEBUSYTIMEOUT to… Convention decisions

litestone replicate, litestone backup, litestone restore, tenancy { } paths, or anything that decides which files an app writesexample: verify:replicate — the only thing that restores a copy and reads it
litestone migrations (autoMigrate, diffSchemas)packages/litestone: test/migrations-fixes.test.ts — and the case that has to stay covered is an unchanged schema migrates nothing, because a constraint compared by text rebuilds on every boot — plus test/migration-residue.test.ts, which is the catch-all under the enumeration: a dimension added to ddl.js and not to the differ reads as in sync, and the row that must stay is the CONTROL beside each firing, since a tripwire that fires on everything is indistinguishable from one that works
litestone import — the four readers and the tier table, src/import/index.jspackages/litestone: test/import.test.ts (the tiers and the marker, plus the guard that every gap('…') literal is graded — which found refusals the corpus had never fired) and test/corpus.test.ts, which is the only thing that puts a corpus of input NOBODY HERE WROTE in front of them. bun test/fixtures/corpus/fetch.mjs regenerates the fixtures through the shipped readers and needs the network
litestone aggregate / groupBy / a @@gate above 5example: verify:stock — availability is a groupBy summed as the shop over rows the caller may not read, and the ledger's 9 for update and delete is the only place a LOCKED gate is exercised end to end
litestone client/policy/gateexample: verify + basecamp: verify, plus sierra: test:safety
junction's litestone write tap (announceDataWrites)example: verify:pay (a transition announced from another service) + verify:live; packages/junction: test/data-write-announcement.test.ts, whose new cases are the shapes a real service file has
litestone valueset / @valuesexample: verify:values — nothing else crosses a declared @@scope from the browser to the boundary, and nothing else can see the ORDER a set declared: it is a directive, so no refusal marks it wrong. The recent(…) head is the only thing here whose answer moves when the DATA does, so it is the one row that separates a derived rank from a stored one
a bulk extract — @@export, litestone export, the manifestpackages/litestone: test/export.test.ts — the claim is that an export is a PAGINATED SCOPED READ and therefore cannot contain what the principal could not read one row at a time, so every refusal is PAIRED with the same call by somebody entitled to it and the row that must stay is three standings, three different row counts from one declaration — a mechanism exporting nothing to nobody satisfies any test that only asks about the refusal. Two more are the design rather than coverage: a batch smaller than the data answering identically to one larger (the export is the one thing here big enough to outrun a page), and includeProtected asserted as a PAIR, since the column is absent and the extract is empty look alike from the reading side
litestone @@softDelete · restore · @keep · @versionexample: verify:revisions — the only place a row is removed and brought BACK, and the only one where two writers race a form
litestone tenancy under strategy database · createApp({ tenants }) · tenantConfigexample: verify:tenants — over Host headers, because a browser cannot set one and the host is the whole mechanism under resolve subdomain. Nothing else separates the DATA, the PEOPLE, the SESSION and the SHOPFRONT
litestone studio — the row browser, the Explore panel, the Models diagram, Overview, the Compare panel, the table dump, the acting-as picker, the Schema Advisor, POST /api/replpackages/litestone: verify:studio · verify:studio:access · verify:studio:explore · verify:studio:models · verify:studio:compare · verify:studio:preview · verify:studio:advisor — the first runs the other six and does NOT short-circuit; it was access && explore, and the stale half hid the broken half for months (FJS-773). Litestone Studio is a served surface with no other drive over it. The six ask different questions: verify:studio:access is who may do what, and is the half that must not regress quietly; verify:studio:explore is the language surface, and it is the only thing that calls /api/preview, which had never worked on a schema with an import in it (FJS-923); verify:studio:models is the DIAGRAM, the front page and the rail — every tier, hue and dimming there is a rendered consequence of a computation, and the failure mode is a diagram that still looks like a diagram; verify:studio:compare is the only one whose input is not the schema on disk, and the only place a value reaching a git command line is graded — the ref is chosen from a list the server enumerated, never typed; verify:studio:preview is the table dump and the acting-as picker, the only one that owns its own schema and the only place FJS-D230's line is executed — that Studio may preview at a standing and must say what graded it; verify:studio:advisor is the one that asks WHICH DATABASE an answer is about, and the only Studio drive that stands up a fleet — a panel comparing the schema to a live DDL is wrong rather than empty when the file it holds is one nobody runs (FJS-993)

The surface, as its README groups it 36

Quick start Working on Junction itself, from a clone of the monorepo: Where Junction lives in an app A FrontierJS app puts one directory at the root per realm, and Junction owns api/: Structure The package itself: The REPL The fastest way to explore a running API. The secret sauce This is the most important file in the codebase. Response helpers ctx.json(data, status?) Methods the transport answers for you Three answers no app registers: Health and metrics import { healthPlugin } from '@frontierjs/junction' Middleware import { cors, helmet, rateLimit, requestLogger, correlationId, csrf } from… CSRF protection The bearer token pattern (Authorization: Bearer ...) is inherently CSRF-safe — a cross-origin page cannot set arbitrary request headers, so it can… Circuit breaker import { circuitBreaker } from '@frontierjs/junction' API versioning const app = createApp({ Idempotency-Key A mutating request carrying an Idempotency-Key header executes once. Bulk operations Bulk patch and remove without an id are disabled by default — a guard against accidental whole-table mutations: Config options Nowhere, ideally. Junction probes two directories beside the entry file — Auth import { createBetterAuthAdapter, createBetterAuthPlugin } from '@frontierjs/junction' Running as somebody ctx.auth.user propagates, so a service call made inside a request already runs Schema validation import { createSchema, v } from '@frontierjs/junction' Service caching Add cache: true to any service to automatically cache find and get responses. Database import { createDatabase } from '@frontierjs/junction' Litestone ORM Litestone is Junction's first-party SQLite ORM. Transactions Multi-step operations that need atomicity — create a user and a workspace together, or not at all — require a transaction. File uploads Junction handles multipart file uploads transparently. Testing import { createTestApp, testCtx, request, callService } from '@frontierjs/junction' OpenAPI app.configure(openapi({ Webhooks At-least-once webhook delivery built on the existing event bus. Scheduler app.scheduler.every('5 minutes', async () => { /* cleanup */ }) Workers Bun threads for CPU work that would otherwise block the event loop. Browser client @frontierjs/junction/client is a zero-dependency browser client for connecting Sierra/Mesa frontends (or any browser app) to a Junction API. Email Junction ships a built-in email plugin with two independent tiers. What is actually mounted The HTTP surface is emergent: services auto-mount, plugins register their own, Tier 1 Plugins First-party plugins built specifically for Junction. Interface-first adapters The blast radius of swapping a provider is exactly one file. Scripts Deploying bun run build:app <entry> (also junction build <entry>) turns an app into a deployable artifact. Dependencies Runtime: bun >= 1.0.0

basecamp's executor (providers/executor.ts), the enrollment exchange (/servers/{id}/enroll in app.ts), or providers/outpost-dev.tspackages/basecamp: bun run test — api/test/compute.test.ts holds the enrollment route, including a SECOND enrollment of one row rotating its key, paired with the old key refused. Then basecamp: verify:outpost, the only thing that runs the launcher and the only thing that asks the executor to choose between two online replicas
an alert rule being EVALUATED — basecamp/api/src/core/alerting.ts, alert-evaluate.job.ts, AlertRule's three condition columnspackages/basecamp: bun run test — the only place a threshold is compared to a series at all, and the only test here that runs a fan-out through a REAL conduit into a REAL HTTP receiver, because a fake one agrees with a body built wrong. Every not-fired row is PAIRED with the same series one value over the line: a fix that fired nothing satisfies any test asking only about the refusals. The row that must stay is a series that STOPPED does not resolve — a scrape that died and a value that came back inside its threshold draw the same flat line, so an evaluator that resolves on no-data closes the incident an outage just opened
a machine's own readings — outpost's src/vitals.js, basecamp's KEPT list, a serverhealth cardpackages/outpost: bun run test — the only place /proc and statfs are read at all, and every reading there is PAIRED with the wrong answer somebody writes first (iowait as busy, MemFree for MemAvailable, bfree for df's own denominator), because all three read as a plausible number. Its other half is one table along and nothing joins them: what the Outpost SENDS and what core/server-metrics.ts KEEPS are two hand-written lists that agreed with themselves for a year and not with each other, so a key added to one is a series nobody writes (FJS-1027). basecamp: verify:screens is where a card draws one. The disk half is one table along and it reads a DIFFERENT TIER: DISKREADINGS is written from the same report that overwrites the DiskUsage snapshot, and cleanup.usage reads the HOURLY FOLD — raw points live 48 hours and the graph spans a week, so a raw read answers nothing happened before Tuesday for every machine and looks perfect on a database written a minute ago. And how full the DISK is is a third wire again — statfs('/') off the heartbeat, not docker system df off the disk report, so a machine can carry either reading without the other and cleanup.usage answers which is missing. bun run verify is the half no unit test can make: absent and zero are the same value to every reader that coerces (Number(null) is 0) and opposite claims on a screen — a sentence saying the machine has not reported, against a green bar saying the disk is empty — so the drive asks ONE machine in two states
basecamp's own production outputpackages/basecamp: verify:build — the built page rather than the dev one: tags have to survive comment-stripping, and a green dev run says nothing about that

Field guide 16

Installation bun add @frontierjs/notifications Schema One model, and it is the app's rather than this package's — the same split Wiring // api/server.ts Writing a notification A notification is a file under notifications/, named for the type it writes. Sending // From anywhere with app context: @frontierjs/auth integration // api/src/notifications/WelcomeUser.notification.ts Execution model notify() formats and validates eagerly, then executes every transport in parallel: The recipient Recipient is { id?, email?, phone?, ...yours }. inApp transport Persists a record to the notifications table via db.asSystem() (bypasses gate and policy — create is gated at SYSTEM, 8). email transport Delegates to app.mail.send(). Requires mailerPlugin to be configured before notificationsPlugin. The address resolves as message.to (explicit… Custom drivers inApp and email are the only transports this package ships. Sierra resource The UI half is a resource file whose data half is <script module>, per Invariant 18 — web/src/resources/Notification.mesa. Querying Standard Junction service — policy scopes all queries to the current user automatically: Errors The first three are thrown before any delivery starts; the last is the only one raised after. Key distinctions method() bypasses hooks, not gates. Out of scope (future) - Notification preferences model — per-recipient transport preferences in the DB

Which file answers which question 11

ARCHITECT.md The mental model and its vocabulary. CLAUDE.md Bun-workspace monorepo: a schema-seeded fullstack framework. DECISIONS.md Dated rulings by the project owner. DRIVES.md What proves a change here, and what to start before proving it. HANDOFF.md The two most recent sessions, narrative. ISSUES_ARCHIVE.md Closed items, moved out of ISSUES.md so the register stays the list of what is live. ISSUES.md The register of everything open in this repo. PHILOSOPHY.md Most of a web application is restatement — the same fact, written five times in five dialects: an ORM schema, a validation library, a TypeScript… README.md A full-stack JavaScript framework built on Sqlite & Bun. VERIFYING.md How you know something in this repo is true. VOCABULARY.md The words this framework defines, and what each one is.

Each one's own opening claim, quoted. Nothing is open unless it is in the register; a settled argument is a ruling and lives in the other one.

CI phases 14

01 hygieneEverything here is about the difference between THIS working copy and a fresh clone.fast
02 structureThe architecture rules, run over this repo's own apps and packages with the same engine `fli check` gives a client app.fast
03 registersThe three registers, graded against the rules they state about themselves.fast
04 snapshotsA snapshot is a generated artefact committed beside its source, so a change nothing else in the repo can see arrives as a diff: the access rules enforced below the API, the DDL every hand-written statement binds to, the JSON Schema three packages validate…fast
05 accessWhat did this branch do to who may do what.fast
06 coverageSkipped is not passed. The aggregate `--filter '*'` walks straight past a package with no `test` script and prints nothing at all about it.fast
07 registryfast
08 advisoriesDependency posture, decided the way everything else here is decided: a phase, not a bot (`IDEAS/tooling-decisions.md` 5).fast
09 scaffoldfast
10 typecheckTwo halves: the direction of the ratchet (a git question) and the count itself (each package's own script already answers that, and exits 1 above its ceiling).fast
11 deploy`fli new` → `fli make:deploy` → `fli deploy:local`: does the deploy pipeline containerize a real app? ~30s and it needs a Docker daemon, so it sits in the full tier rather than the pre-push one.full run
12 mutate`litestone mutate` over each app named in scripts/mutate-baselines.json, its score held to that file's floor (FJS-D476).full run
13 tutorThe tutorial, executed. `docs/QUICKSTART.md` §7 exited 0 on every command it named and had never once put an app on a server — a document with no compiler behind it, which is the failure every other phase here exists to prevent one realm at a time. A lesson is…full run
14 testsSequential on purpose: several suites bind ports and start real servers, and interleaved output from four different runners is unreadable when one fails.full run

Invariants, and what checks them 19

1 Dependency directionLitestone ← Junction ← Sierra, never reverse.attention only
2 Model names are PascalCase singular(model Lead → db.lead); @@external exempt.model-name-case model-name-plural service-model resource-model-miss
3 App layoutdb/ at the root and each SURFACE a directory beside it: api/, web/, site/, widgets/, extension/, desktop/ and cli/.app-layout surface-config surface-src
4 One owner per translation.Exactly one place turns a thrown value into an HTTP status, one wraps/unwraps the result envelope, one parses $-params into ctx.directives, one announces a write, one startup phase list…seam-owner seam-listed
5 One owner per app.<thing>.Claim it with app.claim(name, value); type it by augmenting an exported interface, never by redeclaring the property — declaration merging requires identical types, so a redeclaration…attention only
6 Access is declared in the schema, not in hooks.Gates, @encrypted, @guarded, @@transitions are enforced at the Data boundary.service-as-system gate-unreachable
7 Protected fields are redacted in the audit trail.@encrypted/@guarded/@secret log as [redacted] in field entries and in before/after snapshots.attention only
8 Caller-supplied names never enter a SQL pattern.attention only
9 Patch semantics: an explicit null clears.Test key presence (key in updates), not ??.attention only
10 A $-PREFIXED KEY is transport syntax only.ctx.query is filters, ctx.directives is {limit, offset, orderBy, select}, and no $-prefixed key survives the bridge — one the table does not name is REFUSED there by name (FJS-D237).attention only
11 The nearest delegation root owns an event.Roots nest; a handler must fire once.attention only
12 Mesa compiler output is reproduciblescope ids are content-addressed, which is what makes CSS dedupe work across the two compilers a static build runs.attention only
13 @frontierjs/css is the styling language.Style with a tone (danger) and a treatment (outlined), never a color.css-token-undefined css-raw-literal
14 Typecheck baselines ratchet down only.scripts/typecheck-baselines.json, one number per package; absent means 0.attention only
15 A clean compile is not proof of valid JS.Compiler tests parse their output.command-parses command-resolves
16 Runnable examples are verified, not sketches.A broken one is a bug.attention only
17 Four markdown files at a package root is the standardREADME.md, CLAUDE.md, PROJECTSTATE.md, CHANGES.md; everything else in <pkg>/docs/.package-root-md docs-index
18 In a Sierra app, src/resources/ holds .mesa files, and a resource file carries its model's default form.A Resource is a UI-realm noun, written in the UI-realm language.resource-dir-mesa resource-script
19 A resource file is named for its noun — PascalCase, singular — one Resource per file.App.mesa exporting export const apps; where a model exists the filename IS the model name, so an irregular is visible.resource-file-name resource-one-per-file widget-entry-name

10 of 19 are held up by nothing a machine runs — fli check covers 9. 45 more rule(s) guard a live hazard rather than an invariant. Rules are packages/cli/core/checks.js, run over this repo by the structure CI phase and over a client app by fli check.
